nara_military.1: This entry covers all 30 unbroken 1941 Truppenschlüssel messages on the CryptoCellar list, by net: net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day); net 'nfw', 3 July 1941 (Nr. 84, 85, 86); net '4fc', 8 July 1941 (Nr. 123, 129, 130); net 'f8y', 6 and 8 July 1941 (Nr. 109, 110, 121); net '8be', 25 July 1941 (Nr. 263, 264); June-September 1941 (VHRNE Nr. 284, AOXST Nr. 91, XWFEC Nr. 193, MZXNX Nr. 21, AAXYN Nr. 31, DOLHA Nr. 252, LSSLG Nr. 268, ZUBZE Nr. 8, CFQIB Nr. 281, YSGSS Nr. 56, AFUVO Nr. 26). They were dropped from the 14 Oct Cryptoole import because research/cryptoole/pull.py filtered every CryptoCellar row as Enigma.

sweep_2026-11-16_arabic_2.3: Seen on the SBB scan (PPN618589309, image 467 = f. 231r) by the sweep's vetting, which estimated 120-160 signs. Attempt for the record by Brice Dudout (with Claude Opus 5.5), 16 Nov 2026, comment on PR #706: transcribed twice (same reader, 55 of 59 positions agree), 59 signs of 26 shapes in about 13 groups, so fewer than estimated, and the apparent lamadh-alaph ligatures at the end of line 4 are ascenders of line 5; one test frozen in advance, an abjad key (numerals = letter values, red dot = x10), fails (rank 12 of 201 against 200 shuffled keys, no whole word); none of the alphabets on Sachau 116 f. 1r matches; the Syriac atbash table of Sachau 93 f. 75 was not tested; Sachau 221 f. 20b is a different ('tree') script and a separate lead. Not read. Language (Karshuni or Syriac) and nature not settled: the lines may be a table for reckoning a sick person's recovery, like the instructions below them, rather than a cipher.
